assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organization as a physical-chemical phase-separation problem, linking polymer and colloid thermodynamics to cell biology. Highly original, conceptually clear, and now central to work on membraneless organelles, protein assembly and disease-related aggregation.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granules and nucleoli in 2009 and 2011. Rosen's multivalent-interaction work (2012) gave a quantitative physical framework. Pappu and Mittag made major sequence-grammar contributions, so a three-person prize leaves some credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many labs and systems, and the physical principles are established. The field is still debating how widely biological function depends on true phase separation versus other assemblies, so timing is good but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Debate over which in vivo condensates are truly phase-separated and functionally relevant
Allocation of credit among five prominent contributors, notably Pappu and Mittag
Some disease-relevance claims remain preliminary

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour put to practical use: pH-dependent charge, controlled assembly and endosomal escape enable nucleic-acid delivery. They underpin siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines, with large and demonstrated impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed ionizable lipids, the LNP formulation principles and rapid microfluidic mixing. Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipidoid discovery and delivery. Hope, Madden and MacLachlan were important collaborators. Cullis is the most decisive contributor, with Anderson a plausible second.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale in approved products, so maturity is high. The mRNA vaccine Nobel (2023) already recognised the nucleoside-modification side, so a delivery-focused prize would be complementary.
uncertainties: Fair split between academic lipid chemists and company-based developers
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may influence perceived novelty
My recollection of precise discovery dates and roles is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cell combined mesoporous semiconductor films, interfacial electron transfer and molecular sensitizers in a new photoelectrochemical concept. It was original and spawned a large field in solar energy conversion and later perovskite cells.
assessment.attribution: O'Regan and Grätzel's 1991 Nature paper is the clear origin. Hagfeldt is a major contributor to the understanding and later development, but the decisive invention belongs to Grätzel and O'Regan.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and developed over three decades, so confirmation is excellent. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though commercial impact has been modest compared with silicon and perovskites.
uncertainties: Limited commercial impact may weigh against it
Whether Hagfeldt deserves inclusion
Overlap with a possible later perovskite award

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new chemical modality: small molecules that induce proximity and recruit E3 ligases to remove proteins. It is conceptually clear and has changed drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept (Sakamoto et al., 2001). Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, the basis for molecular glue degraders. Ciulli and Gray built important later chemistry. Credit is spread and a three-way configuration will exclude some strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials, but no PROTAC drug is approved yet. The underlying mechanism is well confirmed, so recognition is timely but the clinical proof is still maturing.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is still incomplete
Choice between PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages
Credit allocation among eight listed names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing enables targeted single-nucleotide conversion without double-strand breaks, by merging deaminase chemistry with programmable DNA binding. It is original and has therapeutic impact, though CRISPR was recognised in 2020.
assessment.attribution: Liu led both the cytosine and adenine base editors. Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors of the foundational papers. Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine deaminase work is a credit question that the supplied credit list leaves open.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation has started and the method is widely adopted, so maturity is good. Prime editing may be better considered together with it.
uncertainties: Whether prime editing (a separate candidate) should be a joint recognition
Priority claim from Nishida and Kondo
Whether the work reads as chemistry rather than biology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory explained how proteins fold despite Levinthal's paradox, using a funnelled landscape and statistical mechanics. This foundation also frames misfolding and aggregation, which is relevant to amyloid and soft-matter assembly.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson formulated the funnel and landscape framework. Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model ideas. Fersht provided experimental mapping but works in a different vein. Choosing three leaves out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely accepted and now supported by single-molecule and simulation work. Recent AI structure prediction does not replace the physical understanding, but it may reduce the sense of urgency.
uncertainties: Credit split between theory and experiment
The 2024 protein structure prize may affect how the field is seen
Which of the several theoretical lineages is seen as decisive

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic-code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allows site-specific incorporation of non-natural amino acids in living cells. It is a clear, original chemistry-driven tool for biology and protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first orthogonal pair (Wang and Schultz, 2001) and Chin extended it to multiple sites and organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed. Schultz and Chin look most decisive, with Wang a plausible third.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used, though its impact is more in tools than in transformed understanding. Many applications are still early.
uncertainties: Whether applications are broad enough for a prize
Relative weighting of Chin versus Wang
Credit for Yokoyama's work

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase, allowing stoichiometry, subunit interactions and ligand and lipid binding to be determined, including for membrane proteins. It is an important analytical method with links to my own interest in lipid-protein interactions.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is the clearest leader, especially for membrane proteins and lipids. Heck and Chait made major contributions to complexes and the method's development. Loo and Gross also contributed, so the configuration involves selection among close contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used and independently reproduced. Mass spectrometry has already been recognised in 2002, which may influence the committee's view of novelty.
uncertainties: Whether the gas-phase preservation of native structure is a limit
Overlap with earlier ionization awards
Fair credit among five names
